Ellie: FYI AcmeCorp is contesting their March private-VPC bill. They were invoiced for a 4x A100 monthly reservation but claim only ~60% GPU utilization. Asking for a line-by-line breakdown. @Samir can infra confirm whether this was a customer-dedicated reservation?
Samir: Confirming Qs 5
Samir: Sorry ignore the noise . Yes, this was a dedicated reservation we purchased for them, not from a shared pool.
Maya: Contract C-7421 attached. Theres no explicit pro-rate language for unused committed GPUs. Legal flagged ambiguity.
Nate: Operational note: cloud reserved instances charge is fixed to our bill; cloud won't refund unused hours. So Redwood faces the cost if we absorb it. Options: pass full reservation through, or amortize against usage and show effective per-hour rate.
Ellie: Finance wants an auditable formula we can show on the invoice. Any precedent?
Nate: WidgetCo (C-6120) last quarter: we showed the full reservation line + an appendix with the "effective rate" calculation and gave a one-time 10% courtesy credit due to onboarding failures. Revenue Ops approved that.
Maya: Proposed invoice lines: - Reserved GPU commitment (monthly) - Amortization appendix: reserved fee / used hours - Actual compute overage - Network egress pass-through - KMS/HSM pass-through - Redwood private license fee (platform)
Ellie: Customer specifically asks why license doesn't drop when GPUs idle.
Nate: Our private license is a platform fee tied to reserved capacity in current commercial terms. We can propose usage-based license, but thats a commercial change and needs Sales+Legal sign-off.
Samir: Suggestion: keep billing consistent but be transparent. Include both (A) billed reservation charge and (B) an "effective per-used-hour rate" so they can see math. Transparency reduces churn.
Maya: Finance-friendly example to reproduce: 
```
reserved_monthly_fee = 28800  # 4 x A100 @ 7200
committed_hours = 4 * 24 * 30 = 2880
actual_used_hours = 0.60 * committed_hours = 1728
amortized_per_used_hour = 28800 / 1728 = 16.67 (per GPU-hour effective)
amortized_per_committed_hour = 28800 / 2880 = 10.00 (per committed GPU-hour)
```
Show both numbers on invoice: the static reservation line and the effective rate in the appendix.
Samir: SQL snippet for the billing view (finance can run):
```
SELECT r.id AS reservation_id, r.month_fee::numeric, r.gpus_committed::int,
       r.gpus_committed * 24 * EXTRACT(day FROM (r.month_end - r.month_start)) AS committed_hours,
       COALESCE(SUM(u.gpu_hours),0) AS used_hours,
       CASE WHEN SUM(u.gpu_hours) > 0 THEN r.month_fee / SUM(u.gpu_hours) ELSE NULL END AS amortized_per_used_hour
FROM reservations r
LEFT JOIN usage u ON u.reservation_id = r.id
WHERE r.customer = 'AcmeCorp' AND r.month = '2026-03'
GROUP BY r.id, r.month_fee, r.gpus_committed, r.month_start, r.month_end;
```
Samir: use NULL handling to avoid divide-by-zero. If used_hours = 0, bill full monthly charge and add note.
Ellie: Can Finance produce provisional invoice lines + cloud-bill excerpts (show reservation charge) by EOD? @Nate add KMS & egress detail.
